Counsel for Applicant :- Mohan Kant Baghel
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Onkar Nath
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
2.
Heard learned counsel for applicants, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.

3. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing the entire proceeding of Complaint Case No. 386 of 2019, Manjeet Kumar Vs. Prem Pratap Singh and others,
under Sections 452, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Kotwali Nagar, District Etah as well as the summoning order dated 23.09.2022 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etah.

entities.text: Manjeet Kumar Vs. Prem Pratap Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted that the opposite party no. 2 is the husband of applicant no. 5, Lalita.

Applicant no.
5 has filed several cases against her husband such as for maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C, for domestic violence under Section 31 of Women Domestic Violence Act and one case under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506, 354 I.P.C and Section 3/4 D.P.Act.
It is also submitted that the named witness in the complaint Jai Prakash is not produced.

No medical evidence is brought on record to support Prem Pratap Singh And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5874180/
1 the version of the complaint.

entities.text: Prem Pratap Singh And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Vide order dated 22.05.2023 of this Court, the opposite party no. 2 is directed to deposit Rs. 50,000/- in favour of his wife i.e applicant no. 5 through a demand draft but he did not comply the Court's order.
5.

Per contra, learned A.G.A opposed the prayer made by the applicants and submitted that witness Manoj Kumar who is examined as P.W.-1 and is an independent witness as well as the informant also have corroborated the version of the complaint.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and after going through the available record,
the prayer for quashing of the summoning order dated 23.09.2022 and entire proceeding of the aforesaid complaint case is refused.

7. However, it is provided that in case the applicants apply for bail within a period of 30 days from today, his application for bail shall be considered and disposed of expeditiously in view of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.
8.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For a period of 30 days or till the applicants surrender and apply for bail, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
